# MCP Skills Extension (SEP-2640): What It Is and Whether It Matters

A citation-backed analysis of the Skills Over MCP working group proposal —
what it proposes, how it works, its relationship to existing skill systems,
current status, and implications for current skill authors.

## Methodology

Research conducted May 2026 using web sources visited in-session. 19
sources cited, primarily from the working group's own repository docs
(Tier 2) and the official MCP community charter (Tier 1). Two independent
review agents verify citations and cross-file consistency.

## Key Finding: The Format Is Standard, The Transport Is Draft

Two things are happening in parallel:

1. **Agent Skills (the format)** — SKILL.md files with YAML frontmatter.
   Open standard since December 18, 2025 [15]. Adopted by 26+ platforms
   including Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Cursor [15].
   40,285 published skills as of February 2026 [15]. **This is settled.**

2. **SEP-2640 (the transport)** — a proposed convention for serving
   Agent Skills over MCP's Resources primitive via `skill://` URIs [3].
   Submitted April 23, 2026 [3]. In Review [13]. No MCP client ships
   native support yet [14]. **This is draft.**

If you write SKILL.md files today, your format is already compatible with
SEP-2640. The question is when (and whether) MCP clients will support
skill:// natively.

## What SEP-2640 Proposes

### The Problem

MCP has optimized for tools. Patterns for how clients discover and consume
other forms of context — including skills — "remain underdeveloped" [2].
Four specific gaps [2]:

1. Server instructions load only at initialization
2. Complex workflows exceed practical instruction size (875+ lines) [2][7]
3. No discovery mechanism for skills
4. Multi-server coordination doesn't fit the single-server instruction
   model

### The Solution: Skills as MCP Resources

Rather than introducing a new MCP primitive (SEP-2076, closed February
2026 [5]), SEP-2640 reuses the existing Resources primitive [3]:

- **URI scheme:** `skill://<skill-path>/SKILL.md` [3][10]
- **Discovery:** optional `skill://index.json` with entry types `skill-md`
  and `mcp-resource-template` [3]
- **Reading:** standard `resources/read` — no skill-specific protocol [3]
- **Capability:** `extensions.io.modelcontextprotocol/skills` [3]

The design is **backward compatible** — no new protocol methods, message
types, or schema changes [3]. Servers not implementing it expose no
skill:// resources and nothing breaks.

**Security model** [3]:
- Skills are untrusted input (subject to prompt injection defenses)
- No implicit execution (hooks/scripts require explicit user approval)
- No elevated authority (skills are instructional data, not directives)
- Provenance visibility (hosts indicate originating server)

### Six Approaches, One Selected

| # | Approach | Outcome |
|---|----------|---------|
| 1 | New MCP primitives (SEP-2076) | Closed Feb 2026 [5] |
| 2 | Registry metadata | Explored [5] |
| 3 | Skills as tools/resources | Multiple implementations [5] |
| 4 | Gateway/composition pattern | Explored [5] |
| 5 | Server instructions reference | Explored [5] |
| 6 | **Convention using existing primitives** | **Selected → SEP-2640** [5] |

The community explicitly cited "complexity fatigue — too many overlapping
concepts (servers, skills, plugins, hooks, agents) erode credibility
and adoption" [5].

## Implementation Status

### What's Working

| Implementation | Status | Notes |
|----------------|--------|-------|
| skillsovermcp.com | Live service [14] | GitHub repos → MCP servers with skill:// + tool shim |
| FastMCP 3.0 | Skills support [7] | Pull model for resource updates |
| NimbleBrain | Consolidated [7] | Atomic repos with skill:// resources |
| skilljack-mcp | Experimental [8] | Tools + prompts + file watching |
| skills-over-mcp | Experimental [8] | Zod validation against Agent Skills spec |

### What's Not Working

**No native client support.** No MCP client ships skill:// resource
support [14]. skillsovermcp.com wraps skills as MCP tools as a workaround
because "not every MCP client speaks skill:// yet" [14].

**Model adherence is unreliable.** The experimental findings report:
"Models do not reliably load or follow skill instructions, even when
skills are preloaded." Adherence is "time-decaying" — models follow
initially then lose focus as context grows [7]. Workarounds include
server instructions directing the agent to read skills first, and
subagent wrapping [7].

### Working Group Maturity

| Aspect | Status |
|--------|--------|
| Format spec (Agent Skills) | Mature — 26+ platforms, 40K+ skills [15] |
| Transport spec (SEP-2640) | In Review — not accepted [13] |
| Server implementations | Experimental — 5+ implementations, 1 live service [8][14] |
| Client implementations | None — no native skill:// support [14] |
| Model reliability | Problematic — time-decaying adherence [7] |

The working group has Anthropic and Google representation at the leadership
and participant level [13], which signals organizational investment but
does not guarantee acceptance into the MCP spec.

## Relationship to Current Skill Systems

### Agent Skills spec is the common layer

SEP-2640 adds *transport* to a format that already has broad adoption [3][12].
The format (SKILL.md + frontmatter) is shared between local skills and
MCP-served skills. The host is expected to "treat them identically, as
though the set of connected servers' skill:// resources were mounted
into a virtual filesystem" [3].

### Claude Code-specific fields don't travel

Claude Code uses non-standard frontmatter fields (`hooks`, `agent`,
`model`, `context`, `user-invocable`) that are outside the Agent Skills
spec's 6 allowed fields [11][12]. Skills using these fields work locally
in Claude Code but:
- Are not portable to other platforms
- Would not be meaningful over MCP (hooks require host execution, which
  MCP skills explicitly prohibit without user approval) [3]

### MCP distribution adds value for server-coupled skills

Use MCP distribution when [4]:
- Skills are tightly coupled to server tools
- Dynamic updates without user action are needed
- Different users need different skill content
- Skills orchestrate across multiple servers
- Ephemeral availability is desired

Simpler alternatives suffice when [4]:
- Skills are standalone with no server dependency
- Single-user, single-machine consumption
- Static files that don't need updates
- Existing skill infrastructure already works

## What This Means for Current Skill Authors

**Nothing changes yet.** SEP-2640 is In Review. No client supports
skill://. Local SKILL.md files continue to work.

**Your format is already compatible** — if you use standard Agent Skills
frontmatter fields (name, description, license, compatibility, metadata,
allowed-tools) [12]. Claude Code-specific fields (hooks, agent, model)
create a portability gap [11].

**Migration is mechanical when it ships** — put your skill directory in
an MCP server that exposes skill:// resources. Content stays identical;
only delivery changes. skillsovermcp.com already demonstrates this for
GitHub-hosted skills [14].

**What you lose in MCP transport:** automatic hook execution. MCP skills
are untrusted input — hosts must not honor executable mechanisms without
explicit user approval [3]. Skills relying on hooks executing automatically
cannot be transparently served over MCP.

## Reflection

Before finalizing: the "26+ platform adoption" claim [15] comes from a
single blog source (Firecrawl) and may count platforms with minimal or
experimental support. The 40,285 skills figure is from February 2026 and
likely understates current numbers. The "time-decaying adherence" finding
[7] is from the working group's own experiments — no independent
replication has been published. These caveats are present in the reference
files.
